items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: For example, you know, he was the chief arranger for Benny Goodman, and we were both scheduled to play at Savoy the same night... Goodman went on ahead of us

ctx.x: Yes, I did for the shows and I did some of the arrangements we played at Smalls. We had -- Al Sears was with us. We had -- anybody that you might know now -- no,

I don't think anybody that you know now, but I did some of the arranging for the band in those days, too, as well as the Apollo Theater. That's about as much as I can elaborate on Snowden. I think it's worth mentioning about another one of our great leaders. I mentioned his name before. I've been connected with Fletcher from his time -- first arrival in New York up to the time he passed. But I remember -- Fletcher made a lot of mistakes as we all have, and they always say Fletcher died of frustration, and a lot…

road. It's 4:00 o'clock in the morning. He said, "I don't care, I don't care." Put him out on the road with his drums, his books and everything, and ran off and left him. So, it was blowing up a storm, so the driver said, "I better go back and get him." You know, when we went back to get that rascal, he's sitting there in the pitch dark in the woods, he said, "I don't care, you didn't have to come." And he wasn't as big as a --
